column1: # The trees this port is pinned to. One `name<space>path` per line; `~` is home.
# IT IS A FILE BECAUSE TWO LANGUAGES READ IT. The pin used to live as a default
# inside harness/pins.py, which meant anything that was not Python had to import
# Python to find out which checkout this port compiles against -- and the Rust
# arm, which resolves its own cites, would otherwise have inherited the box's
# ambient CODEX_ROOT instead. That is not hypothetical: pointed at the shared
# tree, 25 of 35 safari units bundled differently, because the two checkouts'
# An override is SAFARI_COBBLESTONE, a name nothing else exports -- which is the
# property CODEX_ROOT lacks, and the reason pins.py SETS rather than defaults.
